data.body:
**AC3's "percent clamped to 100" is SUPERSEDED by bug `b380-3dfc-99fc-4a0e` (`undefiled-revivable-gemsbok`). The tree no longer clamps, and this comment — not a silent test edit — is the record of why.**

This ticket is CLOSED and its verification was sound: `8629e3874aea` built exactly what AC3 described, and the verifier confirmed it. Nothing here reopens or re-litigates that. What changed is the evidence available about whether clamping was the right thing to specify.

**What was measured after this AC was written.** On 2026-09-05 the production host's `docker system df` reported a Build Cache of 5.875 GB against a `builder.gc.maxUsedSpace` of 5.00 GiB (5.368 GB) — about **109%**, roughly half a gigabyte past budget with 104 retained entries and 0 active. The published `docker_buildkit_cache_used_percent` read **100**. `rebar-docker-buildkit-cache-high` had been firing throughout and was discounted as "the cap doing its job", because a clamped ceiling is indistinguishable from a cap that is holding. The mis-reading survived four measurement passes and was caught only by going to `docker system df` directly.

**Why the criterion looked right and was not.** Clamping is defensible for a gauge whose semantics stop at full — a progress bar, a disk that cannot physically exceed its own size. `container_writable_used_percent` is not that: it is a ratio against a BUDGET, and this ticket's own analysis says the reaper "cannot reclaim a RUNNING container's writable layer at all", so the live set can sit arbitrarily far above the 2 GiB share with nothing on the box able to bring it down. Over-share is therefore the specific failure this metric exists to detect, and AC3 required the metric to be structurally incapable of reporting it. The same argument holds for the other four consumers of `pct_of_cap` (`docker_storage`, `docker_buildkit_cache`, `journal`, `var_tmp`), whose caps are all best-effort targets their writers routinely exceed.

**What the fix changed, concretely.** `pct_of_cap` in `infra/scripts/observability.sh` no longer clamps, so all five `*_used_percent` metrics publish their true ratio. `tests/scripts/test_observability_container_layers.py::test_the_percentage_is_clamped_to_one_hundred` — the test that pinned this AC — is now `test_a_share_overrun_publishes_its_true_ratio` and asserts 300 where it asserted 100; the equivalent tests for the other four metrics were updated the same way, and a new `tests/scripts/test_observability_pct_of_cap_b380.py` pins the helper directly.

**Nothing else in this ticket is affected.** The reaper's safety guarantees, the three thresholds (trigger 100%, stop 80%, alarm 85%), the two state metrics, the dimensionless publishing side and `treat_missing_data = "breaching"` all stand unchanged. `rebar-container-writable-usage-high` is `GreaterThanThreshold` at 85, so an unclamped value strictly widens what it can see and no threshold moved.

Read AC3 as: *the df-derived readings publish from a parseable Containers row and NONE when absent or unparseable; the percent is the true ratio of writable bytes to the share and may exceed 100; the state metrics publish every tick including their 0 path; all five dimensionless.*
